_meta.what_this_is: What is known for this environment and this need, and how well. Not a judgement of safety, not a prediction for a condition without a test. Team computation from NASA PSI tables and quoted documents.

need.question: How long does it take to ignite this material in this atmosphere and flow, and with what heating?
need.reading: A counted test would record the material, the oxygen and an ignition result. No mapped table records one for a solid fuel.

criteria.text: Quantities named for ranking the hazard of materials in the Forced Ignition and Spread Test: time to ignition, fire spread rate, material properties, critical heat flux.
criteria.quote: Develop a flammability test method to rank the hazards of materials used on spacecraft using time to ignition, fire spread rate, material properties, critical heat flux
criteria.title: Strategic Research to Enable NASA's Exploration Missions Conference and Workshop: Presentations (Nahra, ed.); presentations 'Fire Prevention, Detection, and Suppression', 'Fire Suppression and Response' and 'Research Plan for Fire Signatures and Detection' (Ruff) and 'Organizing Questions for Reduced-Gravity Flammability' (Miller and NASA/NCMR project scientists)

criteria.text: The vehicle shall have a fire protection system composed of detecting, warning, and extinguishing devices that do not create a hazardous environment.
criteria.quote: The vehicle shall have a fire protection system composed of detecting, warning, and extinguishing devices that do not create a hazardous environment to all spacecraft volumes during all mission phases.
criteria.title: NASA Spaceflight Human-System Standard, Volume 2: Human Factors, Habitability, and Environmental Health
criteria.version: Revision F, approved 2026-07-14 (Table 6.2-3 also read in Revision E, 2025-05-01)

criteria.text: Rationale of the fire protection system requirement.
criteria.quote: Fire protection is to be based on the anticipated nature of the fire and the likely location of the crew in the event of a fire.
criteria.title: NASA Spaceflight Human-System Standard, Volume 2: Human Factors, Habitability, and Environmental Health
criteria.version: Revision F, approved 2026-07-14 (Table 6.2-3 also read in Revision E, 2025-05-01)

criteria.text: Fire control guideline of the system flammability evaluation: ignition sources.
criteria.quote: The design ensures that ignition sources are eliminated or controlled.
criteria.title: Flammability, Offgassing, and Compatibility Requirements and Test Procedures
criteria.version: NASA-STD-6001B w/Change 3 (Revision B approved 2011-08-26; Change 3 revalidated 2025-06-09, administrative change)

criteria.text: Failure of any one specimen constitutes failure of the material in that test environment.
criteria.quote: Failure of any one specimen constitutes failure of the material in that test environment.
criteria.title: Flammability, Offgassing, and Compatibility Requirements and Test Procedures
criteria.version: NASA-STD-6001B w/Change 3 (Revision B approved 2011-08-26; Change 3 revalidated 2025-06-09, administrative change)
criteria.item_note: Speaks of failure only; it does not say that a pass is limited to that environment (ICES-2014-179 says that, see C02).

criteria.text: Air shall not be allowed to flow during tests.
criteria.quote: Air shall not be allowed to flow during tests.
criteria.title: Flammability, Offgassing, and Compatibility Requirements and Test Procedures
criteria.version: NASA-STD-6001B w/Change 3 (Revision B approved 2011-08-26; Change 3 revalidated 2025-06-09, administrative change)

flow: Air shall not be allowed to flow

criteria.item_note: The standard states no velocity; buoyant flow is present in normal gravity.

criteria.text: Worst-case anticipated use environment: the most hazardous pressure, temperature, material thickness and/or fluid exposure conditions.
criteria.quote: Worst-case anticipated use environment: Most hazardous pressure, temperature, material thickness, and/or fluid exposure conditions.
criteria.title: Flammability, Offgassing, and Compatibility Requirements and Test Procedures
criteria.version: NASA-STD-6001B w/Change 3 (Revision B approved 2011-08-26; Change 3 revalidated 2025-06-09, administrative change)
criteria.item_note: The definition lists pressure, temperature, thickness and fluid exposure; it does not list oxygen concentration (that is added for Test 1 in 7.1.4f). It does not say which pressure is 'most hazardous'.

criteria.text: The worst-case anticipated use environment (most hazardous pressure, temperature, material thickness and fluid exposure conditions) shall be used in the evaluation of material suitability.
criteria.quote: The worst-case anticipated use environment (most hazardous pressure, temperature, material thickness, and fluid exposure conditions) shall be used in the evaluation of material suitability.
criteria.title: Flammability, Offgassing, and Compatibility Requirements and Test Procedures
criteria.version: NASA-STD-6001B w/Change 3 (Revision B approved 2011-08-26; Change 3 revalidated 2025-06-09, administrative change)
criteria.item_note: A requirement on material evaluation, not a definition of a flammability limit.

criteria.text: Ignition delay as defined and reported by the investigators for the PMMA rod tests, plotted against the initial oxygen concentration.
criteria.quote: The ignition delay (tign) in each test was defined as the time from when the igniter was first turned on to the last time the igniter was turned off and a stable flame persisted.
criteria.title: Burning and Suppression of Solids-II (BASS-II) Summary Report (Olson, Ferkul, Bhattacharjee, Miller, Fernandez-Pello, Link, T'ien, Wichman)

criteria.text: Verbatim wording for the existing item EAWG.testing: the ignition threshold data come from a modified standard flammability test and serve to identify materials at risk from increases in oxygen concentration. The report does not say that the threshold is an ignition energy or an ignition time.
criteria.quote: Constellation should institute a modified standard NASA flammability test to generate ignition threshold data for key spacecraft materials. This modified test will allow NASA to identify materials at risk from increases in oxygen concentration
criteria.title: Recommendations for Exploration Spacecraft Internal Atmospheres: The Final Report of the NASA Exploration Atmospheres Working Group

criteria.text: Ignition is measured as a time to ignition, as a function of environmental conditions, with an externally applied heat flux.
criteria.quote: Time to ignition and the time between introduction of suppression agent and extinction are measured as a function of environmental conditions.
criteria.where: External Heat Flux Effects on the Ignitability and Suppression of Materials in Microgravity, p. 24
criteria.title: A Researcher's Guide to: Combustion Science

criteria.text: Properties asked of cabin materials: ignition temperature, combustion rate, explosion potential.
criteria.quote: Materials used in pressurized cabins of spacecrafts must have high ignition temperatures, slow combustion rates, and low potential for explosion.
criteria.title: NASA-STD-3001 Technical Brief: Fire Protection

criteria.text: Design requirements need to specify the pressure and percent O2 combinations permitted in the habitable volume.
criteria.quote: Design requirements need to specify pressure and % O2 combinations permitted in the habitable volume
criteria.title: NASA-STD-3001 Technical Brief: Fire Protection

nasa_questions.text: A response can be defined only as well as the initial conditions of the fire are known: the material burning, the location and size of the fire, and the ambient conditions (O2 concentration and velocity).
nasa_questions.quote: This includes knowing the material being burned, the location and size of the fire, and the ambient conditions (O2 concentration and velocity, for example).
nasa_questions.title: Research Needs in Fire Safety for the Human Exploration and Utilization of Space: Proceedings and Research Plan (Ruff, ed.)

nasa_questions.text: Under 'fire scenarios' the prevention group discusses ignition as ignition mechanisms and sources (oxygen systems, SFOG, overheated cable, short circuits, aging wire, waste auto-ignition).
nasa_questions.quote: Of these potential fire scenarios, the highest research priority was to investigate ignition mechanisms and flammability for pressurized oxygen systems.
nasa_questions.where: Fire Prevention and Material Flammability, Issue 1, pp. 7-8
nasa_questions.title: Research Needs in Fire Safety for the Human Exploration and Utilization of Space: Proceedings and Research Plan (Ruff, ed.)

nasa_questions.quote: Partial gravity levels affect the whole chain of the fire safety strategy, with expected consequences on flammability, flame spread rate, smoke production, detection, mitigation, and clean-up.

not_covered.area: Post-fire clean-up
not_covered.why: Fourth capability area in the NASA fire protection brief; the PSI tables hold no clean-up or atmosphere-recovery measurement.

not_covered.area: Extinguishing agent transport and distribution
not_covered.why: Listed as needed knowledge in NASA/CP-2003-212103; the PSI tables hold no agent-delivery measurement.

not_covered.area: Material flammability in partial gravity
not_covered.why: Named a major gap; every test in the PSI tables is a microgravity test.

not_covered.area: Toxic combustion products other than carbon monoxide (HCN, HCl, HF)
not_covered.why: Required monitoring targets; the PSI tables record carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide only.

not_covered.area: Fire signatures other than combustion gases and smoke: temperature rise, light and other radiation, pressure rise, acoustic waves
not_covered.why: Listed among the signatures detectors respond to; no standard variable of the pipeline (variables.json) holds one of them.

not_covered.area: Transport of fire precursors
not_covered.why: Named as inadequately known in NASA/CP-2003-212103; no standard variable holds a transport measurement.

not_covered.area: Smoke particle size and smoke detector response
not_covered.why: Published by the SAME investigators (SAME.sizes, SAME.detector); the PSI experimental tables of SAME and SAME-R hold the test conditions only.

not_covered.area: Combustion by-products of extinguishing agents
not_covered.why: Listed as needed knowledge (by-products of fires and agents; see also TB008.agent); the mapped tables hold no product reading for a test with an agent.

not_covered.area: Location of a fire in the vehicle
not_covered.why: Named among the initial conditions a response depends on; no standard variable holds where in a vehicle a fire is.

not_covered.area: Transfer of burning debris to adjacent materials
not_covered.why: Part of the Test 1 acceptance criterion; no standard variable holds it.

not_covered.area: Ignition-source control
not_covered.why: Named under prevention in the challenge statement (CH.pillars; read from a copy, not re-checked on the official page); the mapped tables hold igniter settings of single tests and nothing about ignition sources in a vehicle, and need P2 has no counted test.

not_covered.area: Heat release of a fire
not_covered.why: The record says the results 'are used in first order models and predictions of heat release in spacecraft fires'; no standard variable holds a heat release.

not_covered.area: Non-flaming and smoldering combustion
not_covered.why: Named as a gap by the prevention group of NASA/CP-2003-212103 (CP2003.prev.smolder) and in the organizing questions of 2004 (CP2004.flam.q7); no need of this file is about it, and no standard variable marks a test as non-flaming or smoldering.

not_covered.area: Background particulate and chemical species in the cabin
not_covered.why: First organizing question for fire signatures and detection (CP2004.det.q1); no need of this file covers it. The DAFT record (PSI-47) is in the catalogue: its objective field says 'The focus of DAFT / DAFT-2 was to mitigate the risk for the Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment (SAME).', and its table is one row per sampling session, which the pipeline does not map.

not_covered.area: From small-scale experiments to large-scale fires
not_covered.why: Organizing question 5 of 2004 (CP2004.flam.q5); the pipeline does not relate tests of different sample size to each other.

not_covered.area: Detector location and time to detection
not_covered.why: Named as knowledge that detection depends on (TB008.location); no standard variable holds a detector position or a time to detection.

not_covered.area: Flame spread over thermally thick versus thin materials
not_covered.why: Named by the prevention group (CP2003.prev.thickthin); the pipeline carries a sample thickness where the table gives one and does not class a test as thermally thick or thin.

not_covered.area: Flammability limit of liquid fuels as a prevention question
not_covered.why: The limiting oxygen index is named a principal objective of FLEX and tied to spacecraft fire safety (TP216046.loi; see also RG.droplet, FLEX.objective1). The team's scope 'solid' keeps the FLEX tests out of P1; they are counted for S1 only.

not_covered.area: Fire prevention as the stated focus of BRE (PSI-20)
not_covered.why: NASA documents name BRE as the ACME experiment focused on spacecraft fire prevention (ACME14.bre, RG.bre, ACME21.bre). This file links PSI-20 to S1 only, with verdict 'differs', and its table is one row per test day, so no test is counted.

not_covered.area: Ignition delay of the BASS-II PMMA rods
not_covered.why: Defined and reported by the investigators in the BASS-II Summary Report (BASS2TM.igndelay); the PSI-25 experimental table has no column for it, so need P2 has no counted test.
